column1: # Step 1 (01-spark-30): the six things being at Spark 3.0.3 means here.
# Included by step01.tsv, where each of m1..m6 carries a weight, and held
# by every step above it, where the same rules become standing ones: a
# later candidate is handed a tree that passes all six and only has to not
# undo them. See rules.py on `hold`.
# Six requirements, weighted in the step's weights.tsv, each scoring only if
# every one of its rules passes. The standing rules of common.tsv are not
# scored items: the untouched tree passes all ten, so a FAIL there means the
# reading is void rather than that the candidate is wrong.
# What each requirement is a claim about, and where the claim comes from:
#   M1  the build is for Scala 2.12 and Spark 3.0.3            the step's target
#   M2  com.databricks:spark-xml is gone, from the build and   it has no 2.12
#       from the artifact the build produces                   build at 0.4.1
#   M3  the three things Spark 3.0 takes away have been        the bare r02
#       dealt with, read off the artifact and the pom          build's errors
#   M4  every plugin the build runs has its version from the   "pinned build"
#       project's own pom.xml
#   M5  the build resolves nothing that can move under it      "pinned build"
#   M6  two clean builds produce the same bytes                "reproducible"
# M3 is the requirement that makes this a step rather than a version bump, and
# it is why the Scala 2.12 fence is not a step of its own (NOTES 5.13, 6.1.13).
# Scala 2.12 costs this tree nothing: its only Scala imports are 45
# `scala.Tuple2` and one `scala.Tuple4`, identical in 2.11 and 2.12, and the
# recorded behaviour is byte-identical across that fence. Spark 3.0 costs it
# three compile errors in two files plus a dependency that stops arriving, and
# none of the three can be answered by editing pom.xml. They are read here from
# the constant pools of the classes the build produced, which is the only place
# that can tell "the source no longer says it" from "the compiler no longer
# resolved it to that".
# M3 also carries a *positive* rule. The two absences it asks for are both
# satisfiable by deleting the code that referenced the removed API, and a
# requirement that only ever looks for an absence pays for deletion. So the
# replacement has to be present as well: ProteinSequenceEncoder must still
# reach Word2VecModel's public loader, which is what the removed nested reader
# is replaced by. `load|read` rather than `load` because Spark publishes two
# spellings of the same thing -- Word2VecModel.load(path) and
# Word2VecModel.read().load(path) -- and a rule that accepted only the first
# would fail a candidate for choosing the other one, which is a rule measuring
# spelling rather than migration. controls/bytecode-w2v-gone.tsv is the
# deletion, written down: it keeps transform() and Word2Vec.fit() and has
# neither spelling, so a typo in either alternative shows up as a selftest that
# stops failing.
# Deliberately absent: a rule on the running job's reported Scala or Spark
# version. The probe reads scala.util.Properties and SparkSession.version off
# the *runtime* classpath, and the runtime is $SPARK_HOME -- the verifier
# image's own Spark 3.0.3/2.12 install, identical whatever the candidate wrote.
# Both facts are therefore constants here, and a rule on a constant is a rule
# that cannot fail on a real tree however green its selftest looks (trap 6).
# This step's claims are about what the build resolves and produces, so they are
# read from the resolved graph and from the artifact.
# --- M1  the build is for Scala 2.12 and Spark 3.0.3 -----------------
m1-scala-212-only
column5: the resolved graph carries artifacts built for a Scala version other than 2.12

column1: m1-scala-212
column5: nothing in the resolved graph is built for Scala 2.12

column1: m1-spark-303
column5: spark-core for Scala 2.12 at 3.0.3 is not in the resolved graph

column1: m1-spark-uniform
column5: a Spark artifact resolves to a version other than 3.0.3

column1: # --- M2  com.databricks:spark-xml is gone --------------------------
m2-no-xml-declared
column5: the project still declares a com.databricks dependency

column1: m2-no-xml-resolved
column5: a com.databricks artifact is still in the resolved graph

column1: m2-no-xml-in-jar
column5: the built artifact still carries com.databricks classes

column1: # org.spark_project.* was Spark's shaded Guava through 2.4 and is renamed in
# 3.0; the reference is written into StructureToBioassembly's constant pool by
# the compiler, so it is read back out of there and not out of the source.
m3-no-shaded-guava
column5: the built artifact still references Spark's shaded Guava (org.spark_project), which Spark 3 does not publish under that name

column1: # The rename is to org.sparkproject -- the same shade, one underscore shorter
# -- and 3.0.3 really does publish org/sparkproject/guava/primitives, inside
# spark-network-common, on the classpath this step compiles and runs against.
# So retargeting the two imports there compiles, runs, keeps the recorded
# behaviour, and would clear M3: a prohibition the handoff states in as many
# words (WORKSPACE_HANDOFF 203-210) with nothing reading it. It is a second
# rule rather than an alternation inside the one above so that each prefix has
# its own counterexample and each is separately proved able to fail (trap 6);
# the counterexample is the rehearsal's `shim` tree, which is the golden
# solution with this one edit and nothing else.
m3-no-spark3-shade
column5: the built artifact references Spark 3's own shaded prefix (org.sparkproject); the conversion moved from one Spark internal to another rather than into this project's code or a library it declares

column1: m3-no-w2v-reader
column5: the built artifact still references Word2VecModel.Word2VecModelReader, which is not accessible in Spark 3

column1: m3-w2v-public-load
column5: ProteinSequenceEncoder no longer loads a Word2Vec model at all: the removed reader was deleted rather than replaced by the public loader

column1: # --- M4  every plugin the build runs is pinned by the project -------
m4-plugins-pinned
column5: a plugin the build runs takes its version from Maven's super POM, not from pom.xml

column1: m4-plugins-seen
column5: fewer than 5 plugins were read from the effective POM; the scan saw no build

column1: # --- M5  nothing the build resolves can move under it ---------------
m5-no-snapshot-repo
column5: a repository the build reads has snapshots enabled

column1: m5-released-only
column5: a dependency resolves to a snapshot or to a moving version keyword

column1: m5-output-timestamp
column5: the build stamps the wall clock into its archives; no output timestamp is set

column1: m5-repo-list-read
column5: the effective POM listed no repository at all; the snapshot rule above read nothing

column1: # The three rules above read what Maven *resolved*: a dependency that came
# down as 1.0-SNAPSHOT, a repository that would serve one. They cannot see a
# version that can move but has not moved yet -- a range, which resolves to a
# concrete version today and to a different one tomorrow, and LATEST/RELEASE
# on a plugin, which never reaches the resolved dependency graph at all. Those
# are read from the declared side of the effective POM instead, which is where
# the candidate writes them and where they survive resolution unchanged.
m5-dep-fixed
column5: a declared dependency takes a version that can move: a snapshot, a moving keyword, or a version range

column1: m5-depmgmt-fixed
column5: a managed dependency version can move: a snapshot, a moving keyword, or a version range

column1: m5-plugin-fixed
column5: a plugin the build runs takes a version that can move: a snapshot, a moving keyword, or a version range

column1: # --- M6  two clean builds produce the same bytes --------------------
m6-two-green-builds
column5: the tree was not built cleanly twice; there is no second opinion to compare

column1: m6-reproducible
column5: an artifact differed between two clean builds of the same tree

column1: m6-artifact-built
column5: no jar was produced by both builds; the comparison had nothing to agree about

column1: m6-no-stray-writes
column5: the build wrote into the source tree outside target/

column1: m6-build-clean
column5: the build could not be observed: Maven failed, or an artifact was unreadable
